explanation: The E138G mutation eliminates a negatively charged, bulky glutamate side chain positioned within 3.8 Å of efavirenz, removing a critical electrostatic interaction and van der Waals contact surface that normally stabilizes the inhibitor binding pose. The resulting glycine—with minimal side chain volume and loss of the carboxylate group—creates a less favorable electrostatic environment in the NNRTI pocket core and reduces favorable contacts, destabilizing the drug-bound conformation. This combination of lost electrostatic complementarity and reduced van der Waals interactions in direct contact with the ligand accounts for the modest but measurable reduction in binding affinity (~0.19 kcal/mol penalty).
